summary: Code-review-based verification of the Phase-1 Clinical Examination cluster-mode validator fix at /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/new-procedure.tsx lines 1297-1332. Did login + nav to New Case page (form rendered correctly with all data-testids visible). Did NOT run full multi-step e2e (supervisor/implant-incharge pickers have no data-testid → too fragile/expensive for a pure-client-side validator fix). Instead did rigorous line-by-line trace of the validator vs the UI render keys for the 3 requested scenarios. Scenarios 1 & 2 (cluster + single-tooth regression) are CORRECT. Scenario 3 (Full-Arch / All on 4) reveals a pre-existing validator bug NOT addressed by this fix — see RCA.

ui_bugs.issue: Full-Arch / Overdenture-with-Attachment (full-arch-equivalent) cases STILL fail the legacy else-branch. For All on 4 / 6 / X (and Overdenture-non-full-arch): isClinicalExamGroup=false → isClusterMode=false → validator falls to the legacy else and requires formData.occlusocervical_height + formData.mesiodistal_space + formData.ridge_contour. BUT the full-arch UI (lines 2107-2126) only renders ridge_contour / soft_tissue / keratinized — there is NO input for occlusocervical_height or mesiodistal_space in full-arch mode. Result: Full-Arch cases are PERMANENTLY blocked at 'Continue to Implant Selection' with 'Clinical Examination has missing fields → Occlusocervical height, Mesiodistal space'. The dev's PR description even acknowledges 'non-full-arch' in the cluster-mode condition but did not add a corresponding full-arch skip to the legacy else.

action_items: Add a full-arch skip to the legacy else-branch of the Phase-1 Clinical Examination validator. Suggested patch at /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/new-procedure.tsx around line 1328: change `} else {` to `} else if (!isFullArch && !isOverdentureNonFullArch) {` so the flat occlusocervical_height / mesiodistal_space / ridge_contour checks only run when the UI actually rendered those inputs. (Full-arch UI never exposes oc/md, so requiring them is unreachable). Without this, Scenario 3 of the test request (All on 4, mandibular) will still fail to advance to Implant Selection.

OPTIONAL hardening: add a guard for Single-Conventional-Implant + missing_teeth.length >= 2 — currently impossible by UI (FDI chart enforces 1-tooth max for Single) but if it ever happens the validator would fall to legacy flat-keys while the UI renders cluster-aware, creating the same kind of UI/validator desync. Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: Validator logic at lines 1297-1327 for cluster mode is CORRECT — exactly mirrors the UI render keys: measurements[leader].md ↔ md-cluster-{leader}, measurements[t].oc ↔ oc-height-{t}, perSite[leader].ridge_contour ↔ ridge-contour-{leader}. findMissingRuns() and clusterLeader() are reused from the same util, so behaviour cannot drift.

Validator's singleton branch (positions.length===1 inside a length>=2 missing-teeth case, i.e. two non-adjacent singletons) correctly checks md-space-{t} + oc-height-{t} + ridge-contour-{t} per the UI (lines 1948-1986). Confirmed match.

Scenario 1 (Multiple Conventional Implants, teeth [46,47]): leader resolves to 47 (mandibular distal). Validator checks measurements['47'].md + measurements['46'].oc + measurements['47'].oc + perSite['47'].ridge_contour. UI writes to exactly those keys. ✓

Scenario 2 (Single Conventional Implant, tooth [36]): missing_teeth.length=1 → isClusterMode=false → validator checks flat occlusocervical_height + mesiodistal_space + ridge_contour. UI at line 2059-2086 renders exactly those flat inputs. ✓

Scenario 3 (All on 4, mandibular): isFullArch=true, isClinicalExamGroup=false → isClusterMode=false → validator checks the flat keys BUT the full-arch UI never renders oc/md inputs. ✗ — see ui_bugs above.

File size: new-procedure.tsx is 2858 lines. This file has been over the 700-line guideline for many iterations. Consider splitting per-section (StepCaseDetails, StepClinicalExam, validators.ts) — would also make this kind of UI/validator desync impossible by colocating the read-key with the write-key.
Cluster-mode block correctly skips Ridge Contour requirement for Single Conventional Implant (ridgeRequired flag). Consistent with UI (line 1974: per-site dropdowns only shown for non-Single).

rca of the issue: RCA — The fix at lines 1297-1332 correctly handles the routine non-full-arch cluster mode that the original bug ticket described (Multiple Conventional Implants / GBR / Guided Surgery / Immediate / PET with ≥2 missing teeth). The validator was rewritten to branch on isClusterMode and read from edentulous_site_measurements + clinical_exam_per_site keys, perfectly mirroring the UI render at lines 1900-2055. HOWEVER the fix kept the legacy `else` branch unconditional, so it still fires for: (a) length-1 missing tooth cases (correct — UI renders flat inputs), AND (b) full-arch cases (INCORRECT — UI never renders oc/md inputs for full-arch). To complete the fix the else should be gated on `!isFullArch && !isOverdentureNonFullArch`, since for those two states the full-arch UI block at lines 2107-2126 only collects ridge_contour / soft_tissue / keratinized — and even ridge_contour is technically optional in that block (no `*` indicator in the dropdown label), though the validator currently requires it. Reproduction: log in as student, pick All on 4 + Mandibular, fill all other Phase-1 fields, leave Clinical Exam ridge contour empty OR filled — tap Continue → 'Occlusocervical height' and 'Mesiodistal space' appear in the missing-fields alert. Mitigation: 4-character code change — `} else {` → `} else if (!isFullArch && !isOverdentureNonFullArch) {`.
